{{Short description|For 2 disjoint analytic subsets of Polish space, there is a Borel set containing only one}}
{{about|the separation theorem|the theorem on continuous functions|Lusin's theorem}}

In [[descriptive set theory]] and [[mathematical logic]], '''Lusin's separation theorem''' states that if ''A'' and ''B'' are disjoint [[Analytic set|analytic subsets]] of [[Polish space]], then there is a [[Borel set]] ''C'' in the space such that ''A''&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;''C'' and ''B''&nbsp;∩&nbsp;''C''&nbsp;=&nbsp;∅.<ref name="Kecp87" >{{harv|Kechris|1995|p=87}}.</ref> It is named after [[Nikolai Luzin]], who proved it in 1927.<ref>{{harv|Lusin|1927}}.</ref>

The theorem can be generalized to show that for each sequence (''A''<sub>''n''</sub>) of disjoint analytic sets there is a sequence (''B''<sub>''n''</sub>) of disjoint Borel sets such that ''A''<sub>''n''</sub>&nbsp;⊆&nbsp;''B''<sub>''n''</sub> for each ''n''.<ref name="Kecp87" />

An immediate consequence is '''Suslin's theorem''', which states that if a set and its complement are both analytic, then the set is Borel.
